top_problem: This is a very well-made copy of ref-02 panel 1: dark ground, tracked CANTINA, two short columns, and an agave cropped at the lower right. The only part that belongs to Iowa City is a hairline soil line and a root fan, and the root fan reads as a reflection or sunburst rather than loam. The design passes a craft test but fails the substitution test: any agave bar in any city could run this page. The boldest missing idea: make the Iowa earth a real material, a distinct loam field below the line (a value step, furrow rhythm or strata) so the page becomes a cross-section in which Mexican agave grows out of Iowa soil. As it stands, Iowa is a line on a dark page.
remove: The 15-root fan below the soil line. It radiates like a reflection or starburst, adds a second gesture that competes with the rosette in the thumbnail, and does not say 'loam'. Replace it with a loam field, or crop the rosette at the trim.
fixes: Make the soil ownable: set the area below y 972 as a separate loam value (for example a warmer, darker brown with a few engraved furrow or strata lines in the same stroke grammar), so that the Mexico-Iowa fusion is visible on the page and not only in proposal.md; this is the biggest lift for criteria 15 and 16.
Cut the root fan (see remove), or reduce it to 3-5 short roots that the loam crops, so the thumbnail keeps one gesture.

Close the loose header: the gap of about 70 px (18 mm) between the CANTINA baseline and '& COCKTAIL BAR' breaks the wordmark and sub-line apart. Tighten it to about 32 px so they read as one lock-up, and give the recovered depth to the list.

Rebalance the columns: col 2 uses about 60% of its measure while the leaf tips crowd 'Dry-Hopped IPA', 'Dry sparkling cider' and the Wine items. Move the rosette's centre about 40 px right or down, or narrow col 2's declared width, so the art frames the list instead of pressing on it, and the empty bottom-left quadrant under Spirits gets a job (for example the lowest leaf reaching toward it as a lead-in).

Give the engraving materiality: add a slight ink-spread or plate-tone texture only in the art (cut back near text), so it reads as engraved and printed rather than as flat vector hairlines. At actual size the lit-side hatch currently looks digital next to the painterly depth of ref-02.

lens: items and prices against build/draft_doc.json; ingredient names and description completeness (meta.public_components); flow
top_problem: The spirits lines read as database classes, not guest language. 'Blanco-class agave spirit · pour' and 'Añejo-class agave spirit · pour' are NOM-006 class names pasted in, and '· pour' hangs off the end with nothing to explain it. That puts three voices on one page: full ingredient lists for cocktails, three-word adjective lines for beer, wine and cider, and taxonomy for spirits. In the house category of a Mexican bar, the agave pours read the weakest of anything on the page.
problems: All 14 draft items are present and every price matches (15, 15, 14, 16 / 7, 8, 7 / 8 / 12, 11, 13 / 12, 16, 18), with no $ and whole numbers throughout. Nothing is invented or dropped.

The Manhattan hides Aromatic Bitters, which is correct because public_components['aromatic-bitters'] is false. Garnishes (lime wheel, lime coin, orange peel, cocktail cherry) trace to the recipe_versions f06abb74, 14d45e57, 7095fd3d and 9fb77eaa. 'Agave syrup' and 'fresh lime juice' come from the component names. No invented ingredients.

Spirits descriptions: 'Blanco-class' and 'Añejo-class' are taxonomy wording and '· pour' is a dangling serve word. 'Grape brandy from Cognac' is fine, but VSOP is never explained. None of this tells a guest how the two tequilas differ.

The Old Fashioned has house_recipe false in public_visibility, yet it prints the full ingredient list with 'Brown butter-washed bourbon' and 'demerara syrup'. Confirm with Rob that listing named components is allowed when the house recipe is private. Quantities are not shown, so this is probably fine, but it needs sign-off.

Only the Margarita gets an italic tasting note. That is faithful to the draft, but it makes the Margarita look featured without any deliberate hierarchy, and the other cocktails look unfinished next to it.

Known data gap (not the designer's fault): beer has no ABV and no distinct style line beyond the short draft descriptions; Malbec and Pinot Grigio have no region; Brut Rosé has no grape or region; no spirit has a brand. Brut Rosé 13 also has no glass or bottle label, and the 'Sparkling' sub-label does not say how it is served. Guests will ask about all of this, so it caps criterion 8 until Rob supplies the data.

Flow: the reading path runs Cocktails → Spirits (col 1), then Draft Beer → Cider → Wine (col 2). Putting agave spirits right after cocktails is defensible for a cantina. The costs are that Spirits sits at the bottom of col 1 and wine is last, partly in the agave's field, and nothing groups the agave story (Margarita, tequilas) as the house focus. The draft order was Cocktails, Beer, Wine, Spirits, Cider; the reorder is fine but is not explained in proposal.md.

Prices: the inline muted #C4B9A6 figures sit about 1 em after the name, so association is strong. At the same size as the name and in the description colour, they are slightly under-signalled when a guest scans for price in dim light.
'Draft Beer' merges the draft's section 'Beer' with its sub 'Draft'. That is acceptable, but it is a rename to note.
The side-rail and sub-line text ('& Cocktail Bar', 'Iowa City, Iowa') states no item facts. There are no taglines or prop captions, so there is no tagline violation.
fixes: Rewrite the spirits lines in guest language from the same taxonomy facts, with no invented age, brand or 100%-agave claim: for example 'Unaged tequila' is only safe if the class definition supports it; otherwise use 'Tequila, blanco class' / 'Tequila, añejo class' / 'Cognac, VSOP grade'. Drop the dangling '· pour' or make it a consistent serve label for the whole section.

Once Rob supplies the data, give beer 'style · ABV', wine 'grape · region' (and the Brut Rosé grape) and spirits a brand. Until then, keep an explicit missing_ingredients flag in proposal.md for each item.
Add a serve label to the Sparkling price (glass or bottle) once the draft supplies one, and do not print it until it does.

Either get a short draft tasting note for every cocktail or show the Margarita note in a way that reads as deliberate (for example, the house signature), so one italic line does not look like an accident.

State the section order and why in proposal.md (agave-forward Cocktails → Spirits, then Beer → Cider → Wine), and get Rob's sign-off on the Old Fashioned printing named components while house_recipe is false.

lens: Ingredient, garnish and label traceability (build/draft_doc.json, phg.recipe_versions, public.beverage_categories via gateway log 230), description voice, venue fit for a Mexican restaurant and cocktail bar in Iowa City, and how descriptions and prices sit together in preview-letter.png
top_problem: Every fact traces to a source, but the copy reads like a database. The spirits lines 'Blanco-class agave spirit · pour', 'Añejo-class agave spirit · pour' and 'Grape brandy from Cognac · pour' are taxonomy wording lifted from beverage_categories paths (rows 04d72e1f, 9f4dae69, a88f6e79 and bec5063c, all proposal_status 'proposed', not approved). The beer and wine lines just say 'Dry red wine', 'Dry white wine' and 'Hop-forward draft IPA', which repeat the item name or class. So the page uses four voices: ingredient lists, a taxonomy register, three-word adjectives and one italic tasting note. Apart from the agave drawing and two tequilas, nothing tells a guest this is a Mexican cantina.
verified: Margarita 15: phg.recipe_versions f06abb74-762a-4f89-81b2-76a9e4714f3c has garnish 'Lime wheel'. menu_items.menu_description 'Tequila blanco, lime, orange liqueur, agave. Bright and citrus-forward.' is the source for tequila blanco, orange liqueur, agave and the italic note. 'fresh lime juice' and 'agave syrup' come from the draft components cited in round-17/proposal.md. The recipe_components lookup returned null, which is not evidence either way. Glass 'Rocks' is not printed, which is fine.

Manhattan 15: rv 9fb77eaa-c5eb-477c-8e21-acbc89a0e942 has garnish 'Cocktail cherry'. The draft description lists aromatic bitters, and they are hidden on purpose by the draft's meta.public_components (aromatic-bitters false). This is acceptable, but it is the only cocktail without its bitters.

House Daiquiri 14: rv 14d45e57-72fa-4d23-8274-24e5c80e4b12 has garnish 'Lime coin'. The draft says 'house demerara syrup'; the menu prints 'demerara syrup', which drops the 'house' fact the draft supplies.
Brown Butter Old Fashioned 16: rv 7095fd3d-58fb-43f5-8e8f-1a0afadeafa7 has garnish 'Orange peel'. 'Brown butter-washed bourbon' matches the draft's spelling and hyphenation.

Spirits: beverage_categories 'Blanco / plata' (04d72e1f, NOM-006-SCFI-2012 §5), 'Añejo' (9f4dae69), 'Cognac' (a88f6e79, no authority note) and 'VSOP' (bec5063c). No ages, brands or 100%-agave claims are printed. 'pour' is from the draft descriptions 'Blanco tequila pour.', 'Añejo tequila pour.' and 'VSOP Cognac pour.'

Beer, cider and wine: every description matches menu_items.menu_description word for word, and all 15 prices match menu_price. phg.menu_items for project ddc4bb5b also has 'Junmai Ginjo' 12 ('Junmai Ginjo sake.'), which is not printed. The content reviewer should confirm it is not in build/draft_doc.json.
No taglines, prop captions or side-rail copy make item claims. The sub-line '& Cocktail Bar / Iowa City, Iowa' states only venue facts. 'CANTINA' is still a placeholder.
Price association: render_report shows every price inline on the name line, 15 px gap, travel 5%, same_line true for all rows on letter and phone.
problems: Criterion 12: the spirits descriptions use taxonomy register ('-class', 'agave spirit', 'Grape brandy from Cognac'), which the scorecard names as an automatic-fail pattern. They also cite rows that are still only 'proposed'.

Criterion 12: 'Dry red wine', 'Dry white wine', 'Dry sparkling rosé', 'Dry sparkling cider' and 'Hop-forward draft IPA' restate the name or class and add nothing appetising. Only the Margarita has a tasting note, so there is no single voice.

Criterion 13: the menu has no Spanish and no cantina register beyond the wordmark, and there is no mezcal or Mexican-style beer. The section order puts Spirits before Beer, Cider and Wine, but the agave emphasis is limited to one 'Agave' sub-label. The same menu with a different drawing could belong to any hotel bar in Iowa.
Criterion 13/10: 'Tequila blanco' in the Margarita line and the item 'Blanco Tequila' use two word orders for the same spirit on one page.

Criterion 14: the Wine 'Sparkling' group gives Brut Rosé 13 no glass or bottle label, and the beers have no pour size. Under the sub-label system this looks like an omission, not a choice. The draft supplies neither, so flag it rather than invent one.

Criterion 14: prices are the same muted #C4B9A6 as the descriptions and sit 15 px after names of different lengths. Association is strong, but prices form no scan column, and '7' after 'Amber Lager' is easy to miss at 16.5 px regular weight.
fixes: Replace the spirits descriptions with guest language built from the draft's own words, for example 'Blanco tequila, served neat' or 'VSOP Cognac, neat pour', and drop '-class' and 'Grape brandy from Cognac' until the beverage_categories rows are approved.

Ask Rob, through missing_ingredients, for grape and region, beer style and ABV, and one tasting note per item so the beer and wine lines can go beyond 'Dry red wine'. Until then, drop the Margarita's lone italic note so the page has one voice, or ask for notes for every item.

Build venue fit from the draft, not from new items: Spanish kickers under the section heads (for example 'Cócteles', 'Cerveza de barril', 'Vino'), as English-first bilingual headings, and a proposal note asking Rob for mezcal and Mexican beer.

Make 'Tequila blanco' and 'Blanco Tequila' consistent across the page (the item name stays; the ingredient wording follows the draft component), and restore 'house demerara syrup' on the Daiquiri as the draft states.

Layout note for the designer: add a 'glass' or 'bottle' label to Brut Rosé (or a group-level 'by the glass' covering Sparkling) once the draft supplies it, and give prices a slightly stronger weight or tone than the descriptions so they read as prices, not as a trailing word.
